The spelling bee winners were announced and given certificates. A paraprofessional was awarded and given recognition for her work with children with autism. They announced their tentative budget that could cause a 6.69% tax increase. Council Member Wojtowicz- The Wildcat Ridge Preserve, a 123-acre wooded tract in Rockaway Township, has officially been preserved as open space following a sale closing on a project funded through a $1.04 million grant from the Morris County Open Space Preservation Trust Fund. The grant, approved by the Morris County Board of County Commissioners, enabled The Land Conservancy of New Jersey to secure the property. The closing on March 12, 2026, represents the first finalization of purchases involving three open space grants approved in November, authorizing nearly $7 million to preserve 192.3 acres across three municipalities. Council Member Kelley - On March 11th, I attended the Water Department building name dedication/celebration. On March 16th, I visited the areas of power loss, due to extremely high winds, in the Meriden and Valley Road sections of the 6th Ward. During my visit, I spoke with NG Gilbert and Verizon regarding power and communication restoration time frames. I Followed up with Police Chief Scheer regarding recorded data and speeding concerns on Decker/Lyonsville Road [still waiting for the recorded data]. I prepared for and participated in the March 14, 2026 public budget meeting. It was great to see many members of the public that attended. During the budget meeting I made many motions to cut over $300,000 of fat within the budget, increase revenues and public safety. However, the majority of council members were not interested in those areas of reductions to save taxpayer's money. 12. ADJOURNMENT: * NEXT TOWNSHIP COUNCIL REGULARY MEETING – APRIL 14TH*

Home » Meeting Schedule » Meeting Information Welcome to Tucson Unified School District Home Calendar Meetings Search Share GOVERNING BOARD AGENDA REGULAR MEETING THE MEETING WILL BEGIN AT 4:30 P.M. TO VOTE TO GO INTO EXECUTIVE SESSION AND RECONVENE IN OPEN SESSION AT 5:30 P.M. PUBLIC ACCESS FOR EACH MEETING WILL BEGIN 15 MINUTES PRIOR TO THE VOTE TO GO INTO EXECUTIVE SESSION. -One or more Governing Board members will/may participate by telephonic or video communications. -Names and details, including available support documents, may be obtained during regular business hours at the TUSD Governing Board Office. -Upon request, TUSD will provide a certified interpreter to interpret Governing Board meetings whenever possible. Please contact Translations/Interpretations Services at 520-225-4858 at least 72 hours prior to the event. Every effort will be made to honor requests for interpretation services made with less than 72 hours notice. -A petición previa, TUSD proporcionará un intérprete titulado para interpretar las reuniones de la Mesa Directiva cuando lo sea posible. Favor de comunicarse a los Servicios de Traducción e Interpretación al 520-225-4858 al menos de 72 horas antes del evento. Se hará todo lo posible por atender a todas las solicitudes de interpretación realizados con menos de 72 horas de aviso previo. -If authorized by a majority vote of the members of the Governing Board, any matter on the open meeting agenda may be discussed in executive session for the purpose of obtaining legal advice thereon, pursuant to A.R.S. 38-431.03 (A)(3). The executive session will be held immediately after the vote and will not be open to the public. -The order of items on this agenda may be modified during the meeting at the discretion of the Board President or upon a motion to amend the order of business which is approved by the Board. Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. To access agenda items and support materials go to Diligent Community . Recordings Audio-video recordings are available after the meetings on Diligent Community just choose the meeting you wish to view and then select video. Vacancies Events with 3 or More Members Impact Tucson Community and Family Resource Fair - July 25, 2026 Proclamations Resolutions National School Counseling Week Proclamation - February 2-6, 2026 Career & Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation - February 2026 Purchasing Month Proclamation - March 2026 Social Worker Month Proclamation - March 2026 Live Meeting Videos Governing Board meetings will be available here when meetings are in session. August 11, 2026 Meeting Vote to Convene On district Windows devices, students and staff may find that these videos on YouTube are blocked. If so, please log into Google with your district credentials . Error Message: For more details and instructions, please visit our TS Article on YouTube Videos (Sharepoint) . Thank you for your patience, as we work to resolve this.

documents.text: Tucson Unified Governing Board Next Meeting View the Governing Board Meeting Live. Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. To access agenda items and support materials go to Diligent Community . Recordings Audio-video recordings are available after the meetings on Diligent Community just choose the meeting you wish to view and then select video. Vacancies Events with 3 or More Members Impact Tucson Community and Family Resource Fair - July 25, 2026 Proclamations Resolutions National School Counseling Week Proclamation - February 2-6, 2026 Career & Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation - February 2026 Purchasing Month Proclamation - March 2026 Social Worker Month Proclamation - March 2026 Live Meeting Videos Governing Board meetings will be available here when meetings are in session. August 11, 2026 Meeting Vote to Convene On district Windows devices, students and staff may find that these videos on YouTube are blocked. If so, please log into Google with your district credentials . Error Message: For more details and instructions, please visit our TS Article on YouTube Videos (Sharepoint) . Thank you for your patience, as we work to resolve this.

documents.text: Tucson Unified Governing Board Next Meeting View the Governing Board Meeting Live. Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. To access agenda items and support materials go to Diligent Community . Recordings Audio-video recordings are available after the meetings on Diligent Community just choose the meeting you wish to view and then select video. Vacancies Events with 3 or More Members Impact Tucson Community and Family Resource Fair - July 25, 2026 Proclamations Resolutions National School Counseling Week Proclamation - February 2-6, 2026 Career & Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation - February 2026 Purchasing Month Proclamation - March 2026 Social Worker Month Proclamation - March 2026 Live Meeting Videos Governing Board meetings will be available here when meetings are in session. August 25, 2026 Meeting Vote to Convene On district Windows devices, students and staff may find that these videos on YouTube are blocked. If so, please log into Google with your district credentials . Error Message: For more details and instructions, please visit our TS Article on YouTube Videos (Sharepoint) . Thank you for your patience, as we work to resolve this.

documents.text: Calendar Select Board Office Office hours: Monday through Thursday (excluding holidays) from 8:30am-Noon, 1:00pm-4:00pm; Fridays from 8:30am to Noon. The Selectmen meet the 2nd and 4th Mondays of each month (excluding holidays) at 6:00pm in the Bradford Town Hall. Town Clerk/Tax Collector Telephone 938-2288 Office hours (excluding holidays): Tuesdays from 8:00am-12:00am and 1:00pm-4:00pm, Wednesdays from 12:00pm-5:00pm, Thursdays 10:00am-7:00pm. . Planning Board Meets the fourth Tuesday of each month in the Bradford Town Hall at 7:00pm. Office hours are kept by the Recording Secretary by appointment. Email planningboard@bradfordnh.org . Zoning Board of Adjustment Meets the first Wednesday of each month (excluding holidays) in the Bradford Town Hall at 7:00pm. Email zoningboard@bradfordnh.org . Conservation Commission Meets the third Tuesday of each month in Brown Memorial Library at 7:00pm. Brown Memorial Library Mondays from 10:00am to 6:00pm; Wednesdays from 11:00am to 7:00pm; Fridays from 10:00am to 6:00pm; Saturdays from 9:00am to 1:00pm. Transfer Station Wednesday, Saturday & Sunday (excluding holidays) from 10:00am to 5:00pm Building Inspector Contact the Select Board Office to make arrangements to meet with the Building Inspector Emergency Fire, Police & Rescue Emergency Telephone: 911 Police non-emergency number 938-2522
documents.sourceOrg: Town of Bradford

BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS MORRIS COUNTY, NEW JERSEY June 24, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda TIME: 7:00 PM Generated 6/23/2026 3:33 PM This meeting is being held in person and livestreamed via WebEx. The public is invited to attend in person or to view the meeting by following the link below or by calling in to the phone number listed below the link. Public comments are welcome in person or by submitting written comments to the Clerk of the Board, which may be read or summarized during the public portion of the meeting. Written comments may be submitted via email with the subject line “Public Comment” to the Clerk of the Board, Debra Lynch at dlynch@co.morris.nj.us or by mail addressed to Debra L. Lynch, Clerk of the Board, Morris County Board of County Commissioners, PO Box 900, Morristown, NJ 07963-0900. Emailed comments must be received at least eight (8) hours prior to the meeting. Mailed comments must be received by 4:00 p.m. the day before the meeting. WebEx viewer link: https://morriscountynj.webex.com/morriscountynj/j.php?MTID=m2b0d5fc26de6559e3a1e59de5 4299178 Webinar password : grXq6Ht8Dt3 (47976488 when dialing from a phone or video system) Phone number: 1-408-418-9388 Event number/Access Code: 234 409 89132 ANNOUNCEMENT Adequate notice of this meeting held the 24th day of June, 2026 has been provided through resolution adopted by this Board on January 2, 2026 at its Stated Annual Meeting held at the Administration and Records Building, Morristown, New Jersey and by electronic mailing to the Star Ledger and the Daily Record, through posting on the County website and by filing a copy of same with the Morris County Clerk and the Clerk of this Board. DECORUM : The public is encouraged to attend City Council meetings in person or electronically. All persons attending the meeting are asked to observe the rules of politeness, propriety, decorum, and good conduct. Disrupting the meeting may result in being asked to leave or being removed from the building. ACCESSIBILITY : The City is committed to making its public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special/reasonable accommodations please contact the City Manager’s Office at (480) 644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. SERVICIOS EN ESPAÑOL : Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al (480) 644-2767. PARTICIPATION : Members of the public may address the City Council on a specific agenda item or during “Items from Citizens Present.” To speak in person, submit a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting using the kiosks in the lobby or through the City Clerk’s webpage (scan the QR code posted in the lobby). Only one request per person, per item, may be submitted. When called, please come to the lectern and state your name and district for the record. Comments on agenda items should relate to the item under consideration. During “Items from Citizens Present,” up to three speakers may address general issues within the City Council’s jurisdiction; Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on matters raised by speakers that are not listed on the agenda. Comments are generally limited to three minutes unless otherwise determined by the Mayor. If you are with a group, please designate a spokesperson. CONSENT AGENDA : All items listed on the agenda with an asterisk (*) are on the consent agenda which means they will be considered by the City Council as a group, without any separate discussion of these items, unless a Councilmember or citizen requests the item be removed from the consent agenda to be considered separately. To request removal of an item from the consent agenda, please submit a request to speak to the City Clerk prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting. NOTICE : Pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.02, notice is hereby given that the City Council will hold a meeting open to the public at the date and time above. If the agenda indicates, the City Council may vote to go into executive session which will not be open to the public [A.R.S. § 38-431.03]. Members of the City Council may appear at the meeting in person, telephonically, or electronically. Children are welcome at City Council meetings, but please remember meetings are video recorded; by allowing your child to attend, you consent to your child being recorded [A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9)]. ¹ For Regular City Council meetings held at 20 E. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. The Council may move the meeting from the Council Chambers to the first-floor Study Session room if there are technical issues, to ensure the orderly conduct of business, or if there are safety concerns; subject to technical limitations, the meeting will be televised in the Council Chambers and will remain livestreamed online for the public to continue to attend and listen to the deliberations. Visit https://www.mesaaz.gov/government/city-council-meetings for additional meeting and participation information. DECORUM : The public is encouraged to attend City Council meetings in person or electronically. All persons attending the meeting are asked to observe the rules of politeness, propriety, decorum, and good conduct. Disrupting the meeting may result in being asked to leave or being removed from the building. ACCESSIBILITY : The City is committed to making its public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special/reasonable accommodations please contact the City Manager’s Office at (480) 644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. SERVICIOS EN ESPAÑOL : Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al (480) 644-2767. PARTICIPATION : A person may request to speak on the agenda items for Council action or during "Items from citizens present" by submitting a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting via kiosks, QR codes, or with City staff help in the lobby. Only one request to speak per person per item may be submitted. For an agenda items for Council action, comments need to relate to such item, and unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of the speackers is not limited and each speaker is limited to three minutes (if numerous speakers, reductions in time or a spokesperson may be implemented). During "Items from citizen present," a person may speak on general issues within the Council´s jurisdiction, Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on issues raised, and unless otherwise determined by the Mayor, the number of speakers, is limited to three and each speaker is limited to three minutes. CONSENT AGENDA : All items listed on the agenda with an asterisk (*) are on the consent agenda which means they will be considered by the City Council as a group, without any separate discussion of these items, unless a Councilmember or citizen requests the item be removed from the consent agenda to be considered separately. To request removal of an item from the consent agenda, please submit a request to speak to the City Clerk prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting. NOTICE : Pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.02, notice is hereby given that the City Council will hold a meeting open to the public at the date and time above. If the agenda indicates, the City Council may vote to go into executive session which will not be open to the public [A.R.S. § 38-431.03]. Members of the City Council may appear at the meeting in person, telephonically, or electronically. Children are welcome at City Council meetings, but please remember meetings are video recorded; by allowing your child to attend, you consent to your child being recorded [A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9)]. ¹ For Regular City Council meetings held at 20 E. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. The Council may move the meeting from the Council Chambers to the first-floor Study Session room if there are technical issues, to ensure the orderly conduct of business, or if there are safety concerns; subject to technical limitations, the meeting will be televised in the Council Chambers and will remain livestreamed online for the public to continue to attend and listen to the deliberations. Visit https://www.mesaaz.gov/government/city-council-meetings for additional meeting and participation information. DECORUM : The public is encouraged to attend City Council meetings in person or electronically. All persons attending the meeting are asked to observe the rules of politeness, propriety, decorum, and good conduct. Disrupting the meeting may result in being asked to leave or being removed from the building. ACCESSIBILITY : The City is committed to making its public meetings accessible to persons with disabilities. For special/reasonable accommodations please contact the City Manager’s Office at (480) 644-3333 or AZRelay 7-1-1 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting. SERVICIOS EN ESPAÑOL : Si necesita asistencia o servicio de interpretación en Español, comuníquese con la Ciudad al menos 48 horas antes de la reunion al (480) 644-2767. PARTICIPATION : Members of the public may address the City Council on a specific agenda item or during “Items from Citizens Present.” To speak in person, submit a request to speak before the scheduled start time of the meeting using the kiosks in the lobby or through the City Clerk’s webpage (scan the QR code posted in the lobby). Only one request per person, per item, may be submitted. When called, please come to the lectern and state your name and district for the record. Comments on agenda items should relate to the item under consideration. During “Items from Citizens Present,” up to three speakers may address general issues within the City Council’s jurisdiction; Councilmembers generally may not discuss or take legal action on matters raised by speakers that are not listed on the agenda. Comments are generally limited to three minutes unless otherwise determined by the Mayor. If you are with a group, please designate a spokesperson. CONSENT AGENDA : All items listed on the agenda with an asterisk (*) are on the consent agenda which means they will be considered by the City Council as a group, without any separate discussion of these items, unless a Councilmember or citizen requests the item be removed from the consent agenda to be considered separately. To request removal of an item from the consent agenda, please submit a request to speak to the City Clerk prior to the scheduled start time of the meeting. NOTICE : Pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.02, notice is hereby given that the City Council will hold a meeting open to the public at the date and time above. If the agenda indicates, the City Council may vote to go into executive session which will not be open to the public [A.R.S. § 38-431.03]. Members of the City Council may appear at the meeting in person, telephonically, or electronically. Children are welcome at City Council meetings, but please remember meetings are video recorded; by allowing your child to attend, you consent to your child being recorded [A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9)]. ¹ For Regular City Council meetings held at 20 E. Main Street, the meeting is held in the second floor Council Chambers unless agendized for another location. The Council may move the meeting from the Council Chambers to the first-floor Study Session room if there are technical issues, to ensure the orderly conduct of business, or if there are safety concerns; subject to technical limitations, the meeting will be televised in the Council Chambers and will remain livestreamed online for the public to continue to attend and listen to the deliberations. Visit https://www.mesaaz.gov/government/city-council-meetings for additional meeting and participation information. Protecting Youth through Tobacco Retail Licensing Discussion/Direction/Action: Directing the County Administrator to investigate the implementation of a locally administered Tobacco Retail Licensing Program in Pima County - to prevent the sale of commercial tobacco products to young people under the age of 21, who are prohibited from purchasing such products under existing Federal and State law and local City of Tucson ordinance. A draft of such a proposed Tobacco Retail License Program, including draft ordinance language, was completed by the Pima County Health Department originally in 2019 and has since been revisited, with strong advocacy for implementation from the Board of Health, both then and now. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/27/2026

HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, August 25, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 12:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 1:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 Study Session PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC COMMENTS Written comments to the Board of Supervisors regarding the agenda items can be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov. All comments will be provided to the Board of Supervisors. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 9/1/2026

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 9/1/2026

Unapproved Page 1 of 4 Kearsarge Regional School Board 20 August 2026 Open to Public I. Call to Order Chair Mastin called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. II. Pledge of Allegiance The School Board led the pledge of allegiance. III. Roll Call Present : Art Bobruff, Nancy Glynn, Eric Gregoire, David Keith, Paul Lakevicius, Jamie MacKenna, Patrick McGowan, Alison Mastin, and Kristen Schultz. Absent : None Present : KREA representative Catharine Hyson IV. Public Hearing The Board held a public hearing regarding the appropriation of unanticipated funds. Chair Mastin read the following: As required per NH RSA 198:20-b, III, Kearsarge Regional School Board will conduct a public hearing to accept unanticipated funds from the New Hampshire Lead Remediation in Schools Drinking Water and Trust Fund Grant in the amount of $75,000. By accepting these funds, the District is required to perform and use the funds for lead remediation in drinking outlets testing at or above 5 parts per billion at the District’s schools. As advertised in the Concord Monitor of August 13, 2026. Ms. Schultz made a motion to accept and expend unanticipated New Hampshire Lead Remediation in Schools Drinking Water and Groundwater Trust Fund Grant revenue funds for the amount of $75,000. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). V. Approval of Minutes The Board reviewed the previously tabled minutes from the 23 July 2026 meeting. Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the minutes of 23 July 2026, as written. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 7-0-2 (Ms. Mastin & Mr. Keith abstained). The Board reviewed the minutes from the 6 August 2026 meeting. Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the minutes of 6 August 2026, as written. Ms. Schultz seconded. The motion carried 7-0-2 (Ms. Mastin & Mr. McGowan abstained). VI. Reports of Administration The following provided Administrative Reports: Chair Alison Mastin’s Report  She welcomed everyone to the new school year.  She noted that the Board is now full, having brought on Paul Lakevicius, a new Warner representative, over the summer. Superintendent Michael Bessette’s Report For a more comprehensive view, the Superintendent supplies the Board with a detailed Report to the Board ahead of each meeting, available online to the public. The following were touched on during the meeting:  He and Facilities Director Brett Paré attended Warner Zoning Board meeting regarding the results of a variance application, but are awaiting the results, which were tabled.  The Facilities Critical Needs Review process is at the pricing phase.  He commended Mr. Paré for his work on the Facilities Restructuring.  School readiness is on track.  However, he is concerned about several vacancies for substantive positions, including three of the four Associate Director positions.
Unapproved Page 2 of 4  Special Education may require a restructuring, and this is in the works currently. This may require the use of contracted services.  During his report, Ms. Glynn inquired about resources for her to engage as fully as possible as the newly appointed Chair of the Communications Committee and offered to help in any way possible. That information will be forthcoming. Business Administrator Larry LeBoeuf’s Report  None KREA Representative Catharine Hyson’s Report  None (school has not yet begun) Student Representative Cooper Russell’s Report  None (school has not yet begun) Actions taken by the Board: Mr. MacKenna made a motion to approve the review timeline from Superintendent Bessette’s Report to the Board and add it to the website under the Comprehensive Facilities Review. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). VI. Public Comment  Mag Francis of New London : She asked that the Board consider the fact that the discrepancy in numbers has to do with the fact that former Superintendent Fortney would include the numbers in Pre-K, whereas Mr. MacKenna’s data only encompasses K-12. She noted that the NESDEC model is not specific to Kearsarge. She was under the impression that this was going to be unique to the District, but it is a more generic model, which is not ultimately that useful. She also wanted to know if Lavallee Brensinger did something over the past year that was outside the original contract. And finally, she noted that the need to constantly do transfers is a sign of flawed budgeting processes, and asked that they try to fix this going forward. Ms. Schultz made a motion to exit public comment. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). VII. New Business A. Purchase Recommendation- Facilities Director Brett Paré 1. LaVallee Brensinger: This is for a contract extension with LaVallee Brensinger for $110,000. Mr. Paré clarified that the architecture firm attended all the school tours, Facilities B meetings, and were otherwise very heavily involved over the course of the last year. This would require two transfers to cover the cost. In light of the above public comment about transferring funds frequently for large-ticket items, the Board discussed at length what would happen if they did not extend the contract This could include having to start over from scratch with another firm, which would wipe out last year’s entire body of work. . Mr. MacKenna said he believes their extra services were well worth the cost. Ms. Mastin likewise noted that they have previously discussed this pending contract extension as far back as the spring, so it is not a spontaneous purchase. B. Purchase Recommendations- KRHS Principal Charlles Langille 1. FIRST Education Resources-Sole Source-$15,000: Tabled C. Purchase Recommendations- Student Services Director Larry Elliott 1. Staffing Mr. Elliott needs funding for the following staffing and contracted services: Educational Behavioral Consulting (BCBA/RBT): $275,000 Stepping Stones Group (OT): $135,000
Unapproved Page 3 of 4 Boothby Services (ACC, Medicaid, OT, (2) SLP, Teacher of Deaf): $300,000 LindaMood Bell: $34,000 SERESC (Contracted Services): $60,000 Enome-Goalbook: $14,875 EdLaw New England: $68,000 Terra Geer Consulting: $12,000 2. Transfers for Contracted Services: To cover the above costs, he needs to transfer $300,000 into Special Education Contracted Services from Special Education Salaries. D. Transfers & Encumbrances - Business Administrator Larry LeBoeuf 1. Transfers for $5K or less : Every year the Board is presented with any amounts less than $5,000 that need to be transferred. The total for the slate is $101,132.00. 2. Encumbrances : The district has more than $2,011,380.23 in still-open contracts that need to be encumbered from fiscal year 2025-2026 to 2026- 2027. 3. DOE 25/ MS 25 -Board Signature Mr. McGowan was absent at the last meeting and is the only Board member who still needs to sign this document. 4. Fund Balance Approval At the end of every school year, the Board has the authority to retain up to 5% of the budget. Mr. LeBoeuf is recommending 3%, which would amount to $1,410.486, giving $3,347.507 back to the taxpayers. Ms. Schultz recommended that they consider raising it to 5%, but Superintendent Bessette noted that these funds are not easily accessible and could cause a noticeable tax increase. Mr. McGowan said he thinks it’s worth exploring in the next cycle. 5. Bottinger Scholarship-$14,716.44 He needed a motion to deposit $14,716.44 into the Bottinger Scholarship Fund. Actions taken by the board: Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the contract extension with LaVallee Brensinger. Mr. Gregoire seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. McGowan made a motion to transfer $55,000 from two instructional lines to Capital Improvements/Architecture lines, totaling $110,000 to cover the above purchase recommendation. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the slate of contracted and staffing services, as presented. Mr. Gregoire seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to approve the transfer of $300,000 to cover the above slate of contracted services. Ms. Schultz seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the slate of transfers valued at less than $5,000. Mr. McGowan seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. Keith made a motion to approve the slate of encumbrances, as presented. Mr. McGowan seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to allow the Business Administrator to retain 3% of the budget.’ Ms. Glynn seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Dr. Bobruff made a motion to deposit the fund into the scholarship fund, as presented. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained).
Unapproved Page 4 of 4 VIII. Old Business A. Facilities Discussion on Potential Petition Plan for Closure: Superintendent Bessette asked that this be kept on the agenda from meeting to meeting to keep this possibility on the Board’s radar because the budgeting process may overshadow it in the month of September and he doesn’t want it to get lost in the shuffle. Mr. MacKenna recommended having an extra meeting scheduled for September 3, 2026, to give more time to tend to this matter. The Board discussed at length the decision- making process. Ms. Schultz noted she thinks a consolidation to one elementary school with 5 th graders at the middle school is the most efficient way to provide a quality education. Mr. MacKenna asked that Superintendent Bessette have a poster-sized visual for presentation purposes. B. Strategic Plan 2031: Nothing to report at this time other than the Superintendent hopes that the public is noticing its implementation. A summary overview will be provided to the public to inform them of the process. IX. Non-Public Ms. Schultz made a motion to go into non-public under RSA3: II (c) for reputation. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained).  The Board discussed out-of-district student placements. Mr. MacKenna made a motion to exit non-public session. Mr. Keith seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). X. Adjournment Ms. Schultz made a motion to approve the slate of district placements, as presented in non-public. Mr. MacKenna seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to seal the non-public minutes for a period of 30 years. Mr. McGowan seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). Mr. MacKenna made a motion to adjourn. Ms. Schultz seconded. The motion carried 8-0-1 (Ms. Mastin abstained). The meeting adjourned at 8:31 p.m. Respectfully submitted, Amy Monroe, KRSD Notetaker
